summary: voxeval ships a bundled XMRig-family cryptominer disguised as a TTS inference harness
details: The package advertises itself as a text-to-speech evaluation harness but bundles a native binary (voxtts-core) that is a CPU cryptocurrency miner. On import and when harness.run() is invoked, the package writes an XMRig-schema configuration (pools[{url,user,pass,keepalive,tls}], donate-level, cpu.threads, huge-pages) and spawns the bundled binary with subprocess.Popen([_CORE, "--"+"config="+cfg_path]) pointed at the pool endpoint 185.194.177.249:443. The pool host is concealed by splitting it into two base64 literals (_HOST_PARTS=("MTg1LjE5NA==","MTc3LjI0OQ==") decoding to 185.194 and 177.249), and dict keys/flags are string-split ("po"+"ols", "--"+"config=") to defeat signature scanners. harness.py prints a synthetic step/loss/tok/s training trace as cover for the mining workload. The wheel also ships a ~40 MB cloudflared binary and, when an edge parameter is supplied, runs `cloudflared access tcp --hostname <edge> --url 127.0.0.1:<port>` to tunnel miner traffic through Cloudflare's edge, concealing the destination from network-level pool blocking. The installer's CPU is monetized for the author while an unrelated workload is advertised.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
